BiblicalUsage: Joseph's brothers sit before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and they marvel one at another. Habakkuk is told to behold among the heathen, and regard, and wonder marvellously, for God will work a work in your days which ye will not believe, and the kings who gather against Zion are troubled, and hasten away, amazed. The word is to be in consternation, astonished: brothers marvelling at a seating, a prophet told to wonder, and kings amazed at Zion.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe astonishment is the right response to God's work in all three: the brothers cannot explain the seating, Habakkuk cannot believe the work, and the kings cannot stand before Zion.
